chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is allowed to take the pebbles for pelting the Jamarat from all parts of the Haram, except from the Sacred Masjid and Masjid al-Khief.

key_terms.حَصَى الْجِمَارِ: pebbles for pelts for the Jamarat (ritual stoning)
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الْخَيْفِ: Masjid al-Khief (a specific mosque in Mina)

ai.seo_question: Where is it permissible to collect pebbles for Rami during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the permissibility of sourcing pebbles for the Rami al-Jamarat ritual from the broader Haram boundaries, excluding only the immediate precincts of Masjid al-Haram and Masjid al-Khief. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction highlights the sanctity of the specific prayer areas where the pebbles are not to be taken, ensuring the ritual objects remain distinct from the holiest zones. The ruling underscores the meticulous attention to spatial purity in Shia Hajj practices, differentiating between the general sacred enclosure and the core holy sites.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Hanan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is allowed to take the pebbles (for pelting) Al-Jamarah from all parts of the Harram, except from the Sacred Masjid, and Masjid Al-Khief’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il from Hanan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is permissible to take the pebbles for al-Jamar from all parts of al-Haram (the sacred area) except Masjid al-Haram and Masjid of al-Khif.’”
